generators.carrier: unit lower-triangular rational L and rational diagonal D

relations.statement: For a symmetric rational G with L unit lower-triangular and D diagonal, G = L D L^T is checked entrywise in exact rational arithmetic.
relations.hypotheses: G is symmetric and rational; L and D are exact rational data.

relations.statement: If G = L D L^T and every diagonal entry of D is > 0, then G is positive definite, hence PSD.
relations.hypotheses: L is unit lower-triangular, hence invertible.

relations.statement: The certificate polynomial identity (constraints of the fourth-basis candidate = sum of SOS terms from the Gram matrix) holds exactly.
relations.hypotheses: A certificate for MUB6 candidates exists and is specified; currently no such certificate (MUB6-DERIV-073).

lemmas.statement: If G = L D L^T over Q with all pivots positive, then G is positive semidefinite.
Given an actual certificate Gram matrix with exact LDL^T and positive pivots plus the certificate identity, the fourth-basis candidates are refuted.

near_misses.claim: Exact rational LDL of a fixed candidate matrix refutes all fourth-basis candidates.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Such a factorization concerns one matrix only, not a certificate that covers all candidates.

near_misses.claim: A floating-point LDL with positive pivots is a machine-checked refutation.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Exactness is lost, so the reconstruction identity G = L D L^T is not verified.

open_obligations: No certificate Gram matrix exists (MUB6-DERIV-073); it must be constructed first.
No existing declarations were provided, so all references are proposed_new.
The certificate identity linking the Gram matrix to the MUB6 constraints is not formalized.
Lean statements are placeholders and need real definitions.
Whether the Positivstellensatz certificate exists at all for these candidates is unknown.
